version: Task clarity v15: prominent short questions, explicit editable-weight suggestions and named effort comparisons

checks: The reported 43/29/28 → 34/33/33 → 28/43/29 example labels every effort comparison and names its reference test
Comparisons follow each metric identity through reordered runs and distinguish changed weights from unchanged effort
All trio prompts stay single-question and concise while preserving the same optional valid suggestions
Every positive first split has a relevant second-test prompt and a valid optional starting point, without changing the first record
All three adaptive verification routes produce a third distinct player test and a near-even/uneven comparison
Verification accepts player-chosen valid alternatives, rejects irrelevant repeats and zero, and supplies independently copied suggestions
The task is a prominent 24px question card with a four-pixel accent and three finite pulses; hidden time pauses the animation and the card stays readable after it ends
The shorter targeted question and Apply suggested weights button load editable values, announce the result, stop the attention cue and still require manual confirmation
Reduced motion uses one steady outline, and the 320px task card and explicit suggestion button remain readable and usable
The exact reported three-trial example names every comparison baseline and labels increases, decreases and equal effort even when weights change; ambiguous full-cell highlighting is removed
All three records, comparison bases and change labels fit 1366/768/390/320px without horizontal overflow
No runtime errors in task animation, editable suggestions, three actual trials or responsive comparison
All four latest ZIPs are intact, self-contained and byte-identical to their production builds and manifest
The review ZIP contains separate Level 3 and connected Levels 1–3 HTMLs, identical to their tested latest packages
Packaged Level2.html completes 3 → 6 → 10 → 25 → 100 offline with normal motion
Packaged standalone Level3.html completes three player-led tests and compares all actual results offline
Packaged Level1.html includes the latest behaviour and two replies, stops after Level 1 and permits replay
Standalone Level 1 reload starts a fresh Level 1 run
Packaged combined game continues from the current Level 1 into playable Level 2 and keeps sound preference
Packaged combined game connects Level 1 → Level 2 → playable Level 3 in one open run
Combined preview reload starts from Level 1 rather than restoring Level 2
Packaged entries have no browser runtime errors

notes: Level 3 questions now use a contrasting card with a four-pixel accent, 24px desktop/21px phone text and three finite 0.8-second attention pulses. Hidden/off-screen time pauses the cue; slider edits, confirmation, reset or applying a suggestion stop it. Reduced motion uses one steady timed outline. The browser verifies the normal cue ends after resuming from a hidden interval.

Prompts are single concise questions, including What if Participation and Peer response counted more? All 20 trios and representative histories remain within 16 words per prompt. Adaptive purposes, actual effort rules and suggested allocations are unchanged.

Apply suggested weights replaces Show me a starting point and explains Sets the sliders; you confirm. The action loads editable unconfirmed weights, announces Weights set. Adjust or confirm., and leaves Run disabled until manual confirmation. Manual slider edits and reset still work.

Whole-cell highlight fills and the ambiguous data-changed flag are removed. Each table cell explicitly labels First result, Same effort, More effort or Less effort. Headers identify Starting observation, Effort vs First test and Effort vs Second test. Changes refer to qualitative effort, while quiet weight percentages remain visible.

The exact reported 43/29/28 -> 34/33/33 -> 28/43/29 case is checked in the final production browser and component markup. Second-vs-first labels are same/more/more; third-vs-second labels are less/same/less. Reordered metric IDs and large weight changes within unchanged effort bands are also checked.

The browser exercises three actual player trials, suggestion application and manual confirmation, finite/hidden/reduced-motion attention behaviour, then compares all three actual records. The task card and comparison labels are inspected at 1366/768/390/320px without horizontal overflow.

All five latest ZIPs pass CRC and SHA-256 checks, with HTML identical to all four final production builds. Offline standalone Levels 1/2/3 and the connected three-level game pass the actual-package flow checks. The review bundle contains standalone Level 3 and connected Levels 1-3 from those same builds.

The v14 source and downloads remain frozen on archive/pre-task-clarity-v14 at 3ffe53588ef599673228b9156c4af975c5aabd68. Existing archives and versioned ZIPs are unchanged. The prior broader scaffolding, continuous-growth and dialogue suites remain historical in v14 and were not rerun in full for this presentation correction.

Existing authored animation scripts, scene IDs, positive-weight rules, three-trial mechanics, opening integration boundaries and the final theory-placeholder endpoint are unchanged. These functional checks do not establish measured learning effectiveness, direct file opening in the user browser or classroom hosting capacity.
